requirements.quote:
The sender of a stream sends just three frame types that affect the
   state of a stream at either the sender or the receiver: STREAM
   (Section 19.8), STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED (Section 19.13), and RESET_STREAM
   (Section 19.4).
requirements.condition: When a stream sender sends a frame that affects the state of the stream at either endpoint
requirements.required_behavior: The state-affecting frame type is STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender uses any other frame type to affect the state of the stream at either endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation trace can identify sender-emitted frames that cause stream-state changes and verify that every such frame has one of the three listed types.

requirements.quote:
A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state
   ("Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd").
requirements.condition: When the sending side of a stream is in the "Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd" terminal state
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender sends a RESET_STREAM frame for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-aware send trace can verify that RESET_STREAM is never emitted while the stream is in either named terminal state.

requirements.quote:
A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state
   ("Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd").  A sender MUST NOT send a STREAM or
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a stream in the "Reset Sent" state or
   any terminal state -- that is, after sending a RESET_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: When a stream is in "Reset Sent", "Data Recvd", or "Reset Recvd", including after the sender has sent RESET_STREAM
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender sends a STREAM frame for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation trace can correlate the stream state and prior RESET_STREAM transmission with every attempted STREAM transmission.

requirements.quote:
A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state
   ("Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd").  A sender MUST NOT send a STREAM or
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a stream in the "Reset Sent" state or
   any terminal state -- that is, after sending a RESET_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: When a stream is in "Reset Sent", "Data Recvd", or "Reset Recvd", including after the sender has sent RESET_STREAM
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender sends a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation trace can correlate the stream state and prior RESET_STREAM transmission with every attempted STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED transmission.

requirements.quote: The receiver only sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames in the "Recv" state.
requirements.condition: When the receiver sends a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream
requirements.required_behavior: The receiving side of that stream is in the "Recv" state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA while the stream is in any state other than "Recv".
requirements.why_checkable: A frame-emission trace can compare the receiver's stream state with every emitted MAX_STREAM_DATA frame.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame in any state where it has
   not received a RESET_STREAM frame -- that is, states other than
   "Reset Recvd" or "Reset Read".
requirements.condition: When the receiver has not received RESET_STREAM and the stream state is neither "Reset Recvd" nor "Reset Read"
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted, but not required, to send STOP_SENDING.
requirements.why_checkable: The quoted text grants optional behavior rather than requiring an observable action, and it does not explicitly prohibit STOP_SENDING after RESET_STREAM is received; therefore it does not yield a mandatory implementation checkpoint.
